key_takeaways: Library visitation peaked in the early 2010s (~53% of adults, ~3.85 per-capita IMLS visits in FY2019) and declined sharply during COVID-19 (2.01 per-capita in FY2022), with partial recovery by FY2024 (2.53 per-capita).
In 2022, the NEA SPPA (a Census Bureau CPS supplement) found 23% of adults visited a public library in the prior 12 months - the first time this question was asked.
Gallup (2019) found visiting the library was the most common cultural activity, averaging 10.5 visits/adult/year - more than double movie theater visits (5.3).
Women visit libraries nearly twice as often as men (Gallup: 13.4 vs 7.5; Pew: 57% vs lower for men). Low-income households visit most frequently.
Book reading has declined: 48.5% of adults read any book in 2022 (down from 54.6% in 2012). Novel/short-story reading hit a record low of 37.6%.
Print books remain dominant (64% read print in 2025 vs 31% e-book, 26% audiobook), but digital formats have grown substantially since 2011.
The main reasons for library visits are borrowing printed books (64% of visitors), reading/studying (49%), and getting help from librarians (35%).
Libraries are highly valued: 95-94% say libraries improve community quality of life; 66% say closing would majorly impact their community.
There are approximately 133,200 librarians/media collections specialists and ~402,590 core library workers (BLS OES 2024). IMLS reports 143,324 total public library staff (FY2024).

Library computer/internet access serves a critical equity role: ~23% of all Americans 16+ used library computers/internet/Wi-Fi (Pew 2016); 77 million used library computers/wireless (Gates Foundation 2010).
